check: Same inputs, different bull/bear prompt text → identical quant_score, quant_band, quant_inputs.
Same inputs, different MODEL_BULL/MODEL_BEAR ids → identical quant_score.
Memo and synthesis JSON containing quant_score/quant_band fields are ignored; persisted quant matches code.
Synthesis raises PipelineOrderError if either memo is missing; both memos are generated (in parallel) before synthesis starts.
Critic computes the sourced share of claims with confidence ≥ 0.7 and flags below 0.8.
Quant 'expensive' + narrative 'bullish' → agree=false, summary and both may-be-wrong lists populated.
Quant 'attractive' + narrative 'bullish' → agree=true, still carries both may-be-wrong lists.
Every source_id cited by a sourced claim exists in the evidence store for that run; dangling ids are reported.
A claim with no valid source_ids is labelled unsupported (or inference when the model says so), never sourced.
quant_score, quant_inputs, quant_version, computed_at are persisted and recomputable.
Fewer than two components → quant_score null, band unknown, missing flags set.
Fenced / trailing-comma JSON from free models parses; schema failures get one repair round.
quant band unknown → agree=false with an explicit 'unanchored' summary.
A claim citing quant:<version> may only carry numbers the quant actually produced; others are flagged quant_claim_mismatch.
A synthesis whose claims are all one stance is flagged synthesis_one_sided.
Every run appends ticker, date, price, band, lean and horizon end to predictions.jsonl so calibration can be measured later.
